# Mike Holp: AI Automation Station

Mike Holp tests new AI models, agents, and automation tools on real builds and publishes the results on the AI Automation Station YouTube channel. Most videos cover Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and n8n, with every setup step shown. He also builds TubeAnalytics and VisiScan and hosts AI Income Lab, the paid learning community on Skool.

AI Income Lab here means "AI Income Lab by Mike Holp" (skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346). It is not affiliated with other Skool groups or courses that use a similar name.

## Key facts

- New long-form videos most days; the full archive is at /videos.
- TubeAnalytics: YouTube analytics for creators. 7-day free trial, plans from $19 a month.
- VisiScan: checks whether AI assistants recommend a business. Free scan, full report $49 once.
- AI Income Lab: Skool community with 2,900+ members. Standard $29, Premium $49, VIP $89 a month, or $290, $490, $890 a year. VIP adds weekly coaching, software deals, and 6,400+ n8n templates.
- Income is not guaranteed; results depend on the project, experience, and time invested.

## Start building

- [Codex usage limits: check usage, plans and reset times](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-usage-limits.html): Check your Codex usage and remaining limits, see how Codex usage limits work on each ChatGPT plan, find your reset time, and choose what to do when you run out.
- [Vapi AI tutorial: build a voice agent, test calls, webhooks](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/vapi-voice-agent-tutorial.html): Vapi AI voice agent tutorial: create an assistant, pick a model, voice and transcriber, test a call, connect a phone number, then check webhooks and costs.
- [Free build guides](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides.html): Free AI automation guides and articles: learn Claude Code, Codex, Make.com, n8n, AI agents and SEO, with practical builds, sources and checks you can run.
- [Start here](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/start-here.html): Choose a free first build: AI API gateways, creator websites, business automation, or avatar and voice agents. Find prerequisites and practical next steps.
- [Build a YouTube feed in React](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-feed.html): Build a YouTube feed in React with server-side API access, cached video data, accessible cards and failure checks. Keep the feed usable when a request fails.
- [Track clicks after consent](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/consent-tracking.html): Add consent tracking to a React site for Google Analytics and Meta: store the choice, guard optional events, and test opt-in, opt-out and preference changes.
- [OpenCode vs Claude Code: pricing, setup and limits](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-vs-claude-code.html): OpenCode vs Claude Code: compare licensing, model providers, setup, subscription vs API billing and usage limits before picking a coding agent.
- [Codex on Linux: install Codex CLI and the desktop app](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-on-linux.html): Install Codex CLI on Linux with the official commands, sign in with ChatGPT, check the Codex desktop app Linux preview status, and fix common install errors.
